mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, the Exalted, {كَذَلِك يوحي إِلَيْك}: the kāf is in the accusative position as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "with a revelation like that does Allah reveal to you"; in the implied form (the kāf) is placed after يوحي. The name of Allah the Exalted is the fāʿil (agent). Whoever read يوحى as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), the name (الله) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by an implied mubtadaʾ, or by an implied verb, as though He said "Allah reveals it", or "Allah reveals it" (with Allah as mubtadaʾ), or "He is Allah". It is possible that العزيز الحكيم are two khabars (predicates) of Allah, exalted be His mention, and it is possible that they are two naʿts, with له ما في السماوات as the khabar.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {فريق فِي الْجنَّة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and likewise فريق في السعير. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed the accusative for فريق in (ordinary) speech, in the sense of "and that you may warn a party (destined) for Paradise and a party for the Blaze on the Day of Gathering".

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying {فاطر السَّمَاوَات}: it is a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, exalted be His mention, or (nominative) by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Originator". Al-Kisāʾī allowed فاطرَ in the accusative as a vocative; others said it is (accusative) as praise. In (ordinary) speech the genitive is permissible as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ in عليه.

His saying {لَيْسَ كمثله شَيْء}: the kāf is a preposition; شيء is the ism (noun) of ليس and كمثله the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {أَن أقِيمُوا الدّين}: أن is in the accusative position as a badal (substitute) for مَا in His saying ما وصّى, or in the nominative position by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is: establish (the religion)". It is also possible that it is in the genitive position as a badal for the hāʾ in the first or second به; but that is far-fetched, because of what (pronoun) refers back to مَا.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying بغيا بينهم: بغيا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:16-16.t:
His saying {حجتهم} is nominative as a badal (substitute) for الذين — a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) — and داحضة is the khabar (predicate). It has also been said that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with داحضة its khabar, the clause being the khabar of الذين.

His saying {من بعد مَا اسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ}: the hāʾ in له is for Allah, exalted be His mention; it has also been said for the Prophet, upon him be peace.

His saying {إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّة}: an exception not of the same kind as the first (disconnected exception).

[Translator's note: إلا المودة is in āya 23, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {لَعَلَّ السَّاعَة قريب}: قريب is masculine only because the implied form is "perhaps the time of the Hour is near", or "the rising of the Hour is near", and the like. It has also been said it is masculine by way of relation (nisba), i.e. "possessed of nearness"; it has been said: to distinguish it from nearness of kinship; it has been said it is masculine because the femininity (of الساعة) is not real; and it has been said it is masculine because it is construed according to the sense, since الساعة means the resurrection and the gathering, so it is masculine on account of the masculinity of البعث and الحشر.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying مشفقين is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because ترى is from seeing with the eye.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying {ويستجيب الَّذين آمنُوا}: الذين is in the accusative position, because the meaning is "and Allah answers those who believe". It has also been said that it is by omission of the lām, i.e. "Allah responds to those who believe when they pray".

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {وَمَا أَصَابَكُم من مُصِيبَة فبمَا كسبت أَيْدِيكُم}: whoever read فبما with the fāʾ made it the answer of the condition (apodosis, jawāb al-sharṭ), because مَا is conditional. Whoever read without fāʾ, it is on the basis of the fāʾ being dropped while intended; that is good because مَا has not governed anything in wording, since it has entered upon the wording of the past. It has also been said that rather he made مَا in the sense of الذي (relative noun), so it could dispense with the fāʾ; but that makes it specific, whereas if مَا is conditional it is general for every calamity, so that is preferable and stronger in meaning. Allah, exalted be His mention, said {وَإِن أطعتموهم إِنَّكُم لمشركون}, and the fāʾ did not come in the answer.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {وَيعلم الَّذين يجادلون}: whoever put it in the accusative did so by an implied أن, because it is turned away from conjunction with what precedes it, since what precedes it is a condition and requital, and that is not affirmed (as fact). So he turned it away from conjunction according to the wording and conjoined it to the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb before it. A maṣdar is a noun, and it is not possible to conjoin a verb to a noun, so he implied أن, which together with the verb forms a maṣdar; a maṣdar is then conjoined to a maṣdar. When he implied أن, he put the verb in the accusative by it. As for whoever put it in the nominative, it is a new (resumptive) sentence, since conjunction with the wording before it was not good.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying {وَالَّذين اسْتَجَابُوا}: الذين is in the genitive position, conjoined to {للَّذين آمنُوا}.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying {وَلمن صَبر}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is {إِن ذَلِك لمن عزم الْأُمُور}; the referring pronoun is omitted, and the implied form is "that is indeed of the resolve of affairs, on his part" or "for him".

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {يَقُولُونَ هَل}: (it is) in the accusative position as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الظَّالِمين}, because ترى is from seeing with the eye. Likewise يعرضون, خاشعين and ينظرون are all ḥāls from الظالمين, and from the pronoun هم in the second تراهم, in يعرضون and in خاشعين.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t:
His saying {وَمَا كَانَ لبشر أَن يكلمهُ الله إِلَّا}: أن is in the nominative position because it is the ism (noun) of كان, and لبشر the khabar (predicate).

His saying {أَو يُرْسل رَسُولا فَيُوحِي}: whoever put both in the accusative conjoined them to the sense of His saying {إِلَّا وَحيا}, since it means "except that He reveals". It is not permissible to conjoin to أن يكلمه, because that would entail negating the messengers or negating those to whom they are sent, and that is not permissible. Whoever put it in the nominative took it as a new sentence, as though He said "or He sends". It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), conjoined to {إِلَّا وَحيا}, according to the view of whoever puts that in the position of a ḥāl.

His saying ما كنت تدري {مَا الْكتاب}: the first مَا is negation, and the second is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) because it is interrogative, with الكتاب the khabar; the clause is in the accusative position, governed by تدري.

[Translator's note: ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب is in āya 52, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {وَلَكِن جَعَلْنَاهُ}: the hāʾ is for the Book; it has also been said for faith, and it has been said for the revelation sent down (al-tanzīl).
